settings.adjudication: Only rules-terminal games and explicit time/illegal-move forfeits are scored. All move-cap truncations remain unfinished and unscored. Any unfinished game or incomplete schedule withholds the main rating estimate.
settings.clockPolicy: Competition clock exhaustion is a forfeit regardless of remaining mating material; checkmate and time wins are counted separately. Actual wall time including protocol/model overhead is deducted.

caveats: This is a provisional estimate on Stockfish 19’s nominal UCI_Elo setting scale at the recorded test limits. It is not an official human, FIDE, Lichess, or Chess.com rating.

Stockfish documents its UCI_Elo calibration at 120 seconds + 1 second against CCRL 40/4. Testing at 150 ms per move does not transfer that calibration. Systematic scale error is unquantified and is not covered by the interval.

The conservative interval uses entire color-reversed pairs as independent units and the logistic expected-score model. Only four fixed opening families are tested; opening selection bias and departures from the score model are not measured.
Stockfish limiter play may be randomized internally. Recorded source, dependency, model, protocol and binary hashes establish provenance, not bit-for-bit reproducibility of games.
The node cap limits AI tactical work, while Stockfish uses a single native CPU thread and pure go movetime with no node cap. Equal move budgets do not mean equal algorithms or node work.
Per-move limits are soft because synchronous work and UCI communications cannot be interrupted exactly. Equal finite game clocks account for actual elapsed time.
Stockfish is an offline benchmark opponent only, never a dependency of the deployed move chooser.

rating.scale: Stockfish 19 UCI_Elo nominal setting at 150 ms per move
rating.method: Logistic expected-score fit; conservative Hoeffding interval over independent color-reversed pair means
assumptions: Each color-reversed opening pair is an independent sampling unit; dependence within a pair is unrestricted.
Mean expected score follows the Elo logistic curve against the nominal UCI_Elo settings, averaged across the fixed opening design.
The interval covers sampling uncertainty under those assumptions, not Stockfish calibration error, opening selection bias, or hardware/time-control transfer.
